history.critique: Brief & Intent: The three required elements exist, but the core identity promise is broken — the title 'PIXEL DANCE' is set in a smooth anti-aliased heavy sans (Arial-Black-like), not pixel typography, so the screen's name contradicts its own type. The highway 'preview' is empty: zero notes travel the lanes, so the most gameplay-relevant element reads as decorative lines rather than a rhythm-game preview. Clarity & Hierarchy: The primary CTA (START) is undersized, dim, and buried at the bottom edge, competing with the near-illegible 'PRESS [ENTER] OR [SPACE]' hint; the eye lands on the title and then has no clear next step. The right panel shows live in-game stats (COMBO 0, ACCURACY --%) on a menu screen, which is a relationship mismatch — these belong to gameplay, not a title screen. The full-width hard cyan band slicing through the title reads as a rendering glitch rather than a designed horizon, and it severs the sun from the grid. Visual System & Craft: Perspective is inconsistent — horizontal grid lines are evenly spaced in screen space instead of compressing toward the vanishing point, and the outer lane edges don't align cleanly with the D/K receptor boxes. The title's white-fill/pink-bloom treatment is generic neon; the sun is a flat hard-edged circle whose stripe cutoff looks accidental. The START button's notch details are a nice authored touch but are wasted on a low-emphasis element. Expressiveness: The composition is competent but template-synthwave (sun + grid + glow) with no motion, no beat pulse, and no notes — nothing conveys 'rhythm.' Trade-offs: true pixel letterforms risk chunkiness at display size (resolve via crisp hand-built SVG/CSS pixel forms, not a blurry font); adding notes risks noise over the title (resolve by confining notes to the lower highway); making START bigger risks stealing the title's hero status (resolve via glow/pulse and placement, not scale alone).
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (all CSS/inline-SVG, no external assets): 1) Rebuild the title as committed pixel letterforms — inline SVG with shape-rendering:crispEdges or a CSS box-shadow pixel grid for 'PIXEL DANCE' — keeping the magenta glow but adding a 2px cyan/red chromatic-aberration offset and dithered edges so the 'PIXEL' promise is literal. 2) Populate the lower ~60% of the highway with 6–8 square pixel notes color-matched to their lanes (cyan/purple/yellow/pink), animated with a slow CSS keyframe drift toward the hit line; keep the upper highway empty so the title stays the focal hero. Add a continuous glowing hit-line bar linking the four receptors and brighten the D/F/J/K receptor labels. 3) Promote START: enlarge it, fill with a magenta→purple gradient plus outer glow, keep the corner notches, and pulse it at 0.5s (120 BPM) to tie the CTA to the tempo; move the ENTER/SPACE hint to a dimmer secondary line beneath it. 4) Fix the horizon: replace the hard cyan band with a soft radial/linear gradient glow centered on the vanishing point, compress grid-line spacing toward the horizon for correct perspective, and snap the outer lane edges to the outer receptor boxes. 5) Reframe the right panel for menu context — relabel COMBO/ACCURACY as 'LAST RUN' (e.g., BEST 12,480 / ACC 94.2%) so the stats make sense pre-game; keep the keycap row since its lane-color mapping is a strong systematic detail. 6) Final cohesion pass: add a faint full-screen scanline/CRT overlay, align the sun's stripe cutoff with the new horizon, and verify the title glow doesn't clip at the viewport edges.
